text.p: Both naphtha and gasoline prices firmed on Thursday with three deals seen traded for 92-octane supplies, traders said.

Near market close, a Dutch trader sold two cargoes of 92-octane gasoline cargo to a Japanese trader at $23.60 per barrel and a third cargo at $23.80 per tonne free-on-board Singapore. All cargoes will loading between June 4-8.

A European major has also purchased a 95-octane unleaded cargo from Thailand Rayong refinery in a tender that closed Wednesday. The cargo for late May loading was awarded at 65 cents discount to Singapoer spto quotes free-on-board Rayong basis.
The purchases have removed some of the lengths seen in the recent market, traders said.
But some said the recovery may be temporary as more supplies were heard coming from Australia and Thailand.
"The market is still a shade soft," said one trader.
Stocks are also high in Singapore, some traders said.

A slight build in light distillates stocks of 75,000 barrels as shown by the Trade Development Board statistic today brought the inventory levels in Singapore to a two-year high of 7.632 million barrels.
Despite the stock built, Asian naphtha prices also firmed, tracking overnight gains in the European market, traders said.
Traders said the prompt market is weak but the forward month market is healthy.
A western trader said current market conditions are favourable with the weak prices in the May. He said he is short in the prompt market.
India has awarded its tender to sell 28,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha at $53 per tonne below U.S Gulf coast 87-octane gasoline waterbourne quotes.
Sources close to IOC said the company is expected to award two other sell tenders for up to 120,000 tonnes of naphtha for May and June loading on Friday.
In the naphtha swaps market, both June and July were up by 50-cents at $21.70/$21.90.
